chunks: Aban, from Fudayl and Ubayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When death approached Muhammad ibn Usama, the Banu Hashim came to him. He said to them, 'You know my kinship and my status among you, and I have a debt; I would like you to assume it for me.' Ali ibn al-Husayn () said, 'By Allah, one-third of your debt is upon me.' Then he was silent and they were silent. Then Ali ibn al-Husayn () said, 'Upon me is all of your debt.' Then Ali ibn al-Husayn () said, 'Indeed, what prevented me from assuming it for him initially was the dislike that they would say,
ai.seo_question: Why did Ali ibn al-Husayn hesitate before offering to pay the full debt?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the virtue of *ikhlas* (sincerity) and humility in charitable acts, illustrating how Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) prioritized avoiding *riya* (ostentation) over immediate recognition. His initial silence and subsequent full assumption of the debt demonstrate the Shia scholarly emphasis on internal purity of intention over external social dynamics among the Ahl al-Bayt. This narrative serves as a practical model for believers to ensure their generosity is solely for God’s pleasure rather than for gaining precedence or status among peers.

en.hubeali: H 14962 – Aban, from Fazeyl and Ubeyd, who has said: Abu Abdullahasws has said:

‘When the death presented itself to Muhammad Bin Usama, the Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup> came up to him. So he said to them, ‘You have recognised my being near in relations to you, and my status among you, and I have a debt upon me so I would love it if you could take the responsibility of it from me’. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, a third of your debt is upon me<sup>asws</sup>’, then he<sup>asws</sup> was quiet and they remained quiet. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon me<sup>asws</sup> is all of your debt’. Then Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But what prevented me<sup>asws</sup> from assuming the responsibility of all of his debts at first was the abhorrence that they would say, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> preceded us for it’.
en.sarwar: 515. Aban, from Abu Baseer, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said:

‘Whenever the Rasool Allah (saww) descended from his (saww) she-camel Al-Qaswa, he (saww) would leave its reins upon it. It would go out and come to the Muslims. So this man would give it something, and that man would give it something. So it would not remain without (its hunger) is being satisfied. It entered its head in a tent of Samarat Bin Jundab, so he took hold of a stick and struck it upon its head. So he scratched it. So it went out to the Prophet (saww) and complained to him (saww)’.
